title: Windows reports Godot as "Not Responding" after about 5 seconds of inactivity (4.7.2 / 4.8-dev7)
body: ### Tested versions Tested on the same PC: - Godot 4.7.1 stable: Remained Running for more than 30 seconds. - Godot 4.7.2 stable: Task Manager shows Not Responding after about 5 seconds without interaction. - Godot 4.8-dev7 (c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f): Initially shows Running after startup. After clicking once inside the Project Manager, it becomes Not Responding following about 5 seconds of inactivity. ### System information Godot v4.7.2.stable Windows 11 build 26200 OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti NVIDIA driver 32.0.16.1714 AMD Ryzen 7 5700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) 31.92 GiB memory 1 monitor / Multi-window WASAPI 48000 Hz ### Issue description I used AI tools to automate test execution, build engine variants, and create a standalone Win32 test program. I personally checked the behavior in Task Manager and performed the manual interaction tests. The English version was machine-translated from the original Japanese text. Measurement logs are available on request. While developing a game, I noticed that Windows was reporting the Godot window as Not Responding. At first, I thought the problem was with my game. However, after narrowing it down, I found that it could be reproduced simply by launching Godot's Project Manager, without even opening a project. I compared the Windows-side code in 4.7.1 and 4.7.2 and investigated the possible connection to the message pump / raw input changes in PR #109639. With 4.7.2, restoring only the message pump to the 4.7.1-style implementation prevented the Hung classification in my tests. Removing only DisableProcessWindowsGhosting() did not help. In a simple standalone Win32 test without Godot, a filtered message pump also reproduced the Hung classification after about 5 seconds, while an unfiltered pump did not. However, in one test with the 4.7.1-style message pump restored in 4.8-dev7, the window was still classified as Hung after about 6 seconds. Therefore, I have not identified the root cause or a general fix. In separate automated tests using an empty project with Godot 4.7.2 and 4.8-dev7, the process / physics / render counters continued to advance while Windows reported the window as Hung. Both versions also responded to SendMessageTimeout(WM_NULL). The attached screenshot is from Windows Task Manager in Japanese. The Japanese labels in the Status column mean: - "実行中" = Running - "応答なし" = Not Responding ### Steps to reproduce 1. Launch Godot 4.7.2 on Windows. 2. Leave it at the Project Manager without opening any project. 3. Wait about 5 seconds without interacting with it. 4. Check the state of the Godot process in the Details tab of Windows Task Manager. 5. It shows "Not Responding". 6. Click inside the Project Manager window. The state returns to "Running". 7. Leave it alone for about 5 seconds again, and it returns to "Not Responding". For comparison, I did not observe this behavior in 4.7.1 for more than 30 seconds on the same PC. In 4.8-dev7, it did not occur immediately after startup, but after clicking once inside the Project Manager, it entered the same state as 4.7.2. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A No MRP is needed because the issue reproduces in the Project Manager before opening any project.
